title: Cities
objective: After this level you can explain why cities grow and name the largest urban areas.
summary: Cities pull people in with jobs and opportunity, and boomed with industry. Megacities (10 million+) grew from 8 to 33; by the UN's 2025 count Jakarta, Dhaka and Tokyo are the largest.

cards.headline: Tokyo was long the world's biggest city. Then the UN measured again.
cards.body: In 2025 a UN report crowned Jakarta instead, using a new method. Nobody packed a single moving box that day. So how do cities grow, and how do you even measure one?

cards.headline: Why cities pull people in
cards.body: Cities work like magnets. People leave the countryside for jobs in factories and offices, and for better chances at school and a livelier life. Cities really began to boom in the 18th century, when large-scale industry arrived. Factories needed workers, and the workers came. That's how a market town becomes a skyline.

cards.fact: In 1975 the world had 8 megacities. By 2025 it had 33.
cards.context: A megacity is an urban area with 10 million people or more. Of today's 33, 19 are in Asia, which fits Level 91: the Asia-Pacific region is home to about 60% of humanity. Picture an entire country's worth of people sharing one subway map.

cards.headline: Where does a city end?
cards.body: Measuring a city sounds easy until you try to find its edge. Countries used to draw that line in different ways, so the UN's 2025 figures switched to one shared method. By that count, Jakarta leads with nearly 42 million people, Dhaka has almost 40 million and Tokyo 33 million. Dhaka is projected to take first place by 2050. City rankings, like milk, come with a date on them.

mascot.line: This is Level 3's meridian problem again: nothing compares until everyone measures the same way.

cards.headline: Cities: mapped
learned: Jobs and opportunity pull people into cities
Megacities have 10 million+ people: 8 in 1975, 33 in 2025
By the UN's 2025 count: Jakarta, Dhaka, Tokyo

questions.prompt: What makes an urban area a megacity?

options.label: Having more than 100 skyscrapers
options.rationale: Buildings do not define it; people do.

options.label: Spreading across two countries
options.rationale: Borders have nothing to do with it.

questions.explanation: A megacity is an urban area with 10 million or more inhabitants. There were 33 in 2025.

questions.prompt: What mainly pulls people from the countryside into cities?

options.label: Jobs, plus better chances for education
Cheaper housing than in villages
options.rationale: City housing is rarely the draw.

options.label: Cooler weather
options.rationale: Climate is not what drives urban growth.

options.label: Laws that require it
options.rationale: People move by choice, for opportunity.

questions.explanation: Cities draw people with jobs in manufacturing and the professions and with chances for education and entertainment.

questions.prompt: From Level 65: about three in five people live on one continent. Which continent holds most of today's megacities?

options.label: Africa
options.rationale: Most of the 33 are on the continent with the most people.

options.label: Europe
options.rationale: Only a small share of the 33 are there.

options.label: North America
options.rationale: Only a small share of the 33 are there.

questions.explanation: Asia is home to about three-fifths of the world's people, and 19 of the 33 megacities are there.
